name: Sihanouk International Airport
before:
Cambodia's third international airport, 20 km east of Sihanoukville and the way in for the southern coast and islands. It is named, like the province, after King Norodom Sihanouk, and is also known as Kang Keng. The code KOS comes from Kampong Som, the town's other name.

The runway is 3,300 metres and takes large aircraft, with five stands and a full set of navigation aids. Rescue and firefighting cover is at ICAO category 5.

Its history has been stop and start. The airfield was built in the 1960s with Soviet help, then lay dormant through the Khmer Rouge years and long after. It formally reopened in January 2007 with a lengthened runway and widened taxiways, but scheduled flights stopped again after an accident that June and did not return until December 2011, when Cambodia Angkor Air began flying from Siem Reap. A triangle route linking Siem Reap, Sihanoukville and Phnom Penh followed in 2013.
